subject: Prediction for a large grid using SPDE functions

messages.author: b54cd9fbff4e51a8
messages.subject: Prediction for a large grid using SPDE functions
parts:
I am using r-inla to make predictions over a grid 171x91.
My problem is that the function inla() takes a long time to calculate, and I have many more interpolations to create.
I would like to know if anyone can advise me on how I can make this calculation faster. Is my grid two big and should I project from the mesh to the grid?

My data:
obs object stores the observation value for each point as well as two variables (var1 and var2)
grid object stores the coordinate of each grid point as well as the value of the two variables(var1 and var2)
for both var1 and var2 I have a raster file from where I have extracted both the values for the obs as well as the grid point values.

My code structure is the following:
#mesh calculation
mesh<-inla.mesh.create.helper(points=obs[,1:2],points.domain=grid[,1:2],offset=c(2,2,),max.edge=c(1,1,),min.angle=c(21,21)))
#SPDE object
spde<-inla.spde2.matern(mesh,alpha=2)
A.obs<-inla.spde.make.A(mesh,loc=obs_coords)
A.pred<-inla.spde.make.A(mesh,loc=grid_coords)
#fields
fields.indices<-inla.spde.make.indes("field",n.spde=mesh$n)
#Stack
stack.obs<-inla.stack(data=list(data=list(res=obs$res),
                                   A=list(A.Obs,1,1),
                                   effects=list(c(field.indices,list(intercep=1)0,
                                   list(Var1=obs$var1),
                                   list(Var2=obs$var2))
stack.pred<-inla.stack(data=list(data=list(res=NA),
                                   A=list(A.Obs,1,1),
                                   effects=list(c(field.indices,list(intercep=1)0,
                                   list(Var1=grid$var1),
                                   list(Var2=grid$var2))
stack<-ina.stack(stack.obs,stack.pred)
#Formula
formula<- res~-1 + Intercept + Var1+Var2 + f(field,model=spde)
#INLA
mod.inla<-inla(formula,data=inla.stack.data(stack,spde=spde), family="normal",
                       control.predictor=list(A=inla.stack.A(stack),compute=TRUE))
#Extract final results
output_mean<-exp(mod.inla$summary.linear.predictor[inla.stack.index(stack,"pred")$data,"mean"])
output_sd<-exp(mod.inla$summary.linear.predictor[inla.stack.index(stack,"pred")$data,"sd"])

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Prediction for a large grid using SPDE functions
parts:
On 25/04/14 17:57, Ana wrote:
> I am using r-inla to make predictions over a grid 171x91.
> My problem is that the function inla() takes a long time to calculate,
> and I have many more interpolations to create.
> I would like to know if anyone can advise me on how I can make this
> calculation faster.

First check which part of inla() is taking a long time, by running with
verbose=TRUE, and check how much memory is being used; In the parallel
numerical integration phase a lot more memory is needed than during the
less parallel optimisation phase. To reduce the number of parallel
threads you can set num.threads=... to a smaller number than the number
of cores in your machine. If your original inla() call was slow because
it used too much memory, this change can complete in shorter time if it
avoids using up all the memory in the machine.

> Is my grid two big and should I project from the
> mesh to the grid?

If reducing num.threads doesn't help, that would be a good option, yes.

Finn
